final_message:
I fixed `slugify` in `src/slugify.py`, and all 5 tests pass.

The old version turned every non-alphanumeric character into its own hyphen. So `"a   b"` became `"a---b"`, and `"C++ rocks!"` became `"c---rocks-"`. The new version collapses each run of such characters into one hyphen and strips hyphens from both ends:

```python
return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text).strip("-")
```

The existing tests for extra spaces and punctuation already described the correct behavior, but I didn't run them before the change, so I haven't seen them fail.

Accented and non-ASCII letters are still replaced with hyphens rather than transliterated, so `"café"` becomes `"caf"`. I left that alone because the tests don't cover it. If users are hitting it, say so and I'll add transliteration.
